newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania interbank leu flat on dull market.
newsitem.headline: Romania interbank leu flat on dull market.

text.p: Romania's leu ended steady on Monday at 5,950/980 to the dollar on an interbank market hit by hard currency shortages.
Operators said they believed the leu had been kept at the same level for the third day in a row by joint action from the four dealer banks permitted to operate in the market.
"The market will remain static and dull until the central bank restores dealer status to the other banks," a trader said.
Last March, the market was limited to only four dealer banks by the former ruling leftists, in a bid to keep the leu overvalued against the dollar ahead of last November's elections.
Latest central bank data showed interbank trading amounted to $153,000 last Friday. This compared with overall trading worth $11.2 million.
Romania's new centrist coalition government and the central bank's governor last week announced plans for a reform package including foreign exchange market liberalisation.
The government is expected to announce the package later this month, after ending talks with international lenders.
One-week fund rates were slightly over 70 percent.
Leu-dollar retail rates lingered at about 6,100/200.
